title: Viewport texture repeat inheritance incorrectly falls back to Disabled
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: - v4.8.dev5.official [9552dfb68] - v4.7.2.stable.steam [ed1daf0bf] ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1088) - AMD Ryzen 9 7940HX with Radeon Graphics (32 threads) - 31.21 GiB memory - WASAPI (96000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description I set Default Texture Repeat to Enabled in the project settings, but a Sprite2D inside a SubViewport still stretches the texture's edges instead of repeating it. The scene is just SubViewportContainer -> SubViewport -> Sprite2D, with texture repeat set to Inherit on all three nodes. I'd expect this to use the project's Enabled setting. Changing the SubViewport's repeat mode from Inherit to Enabled makes it work. Leaving it on Inherit and setting the SubViewportContainer's repeat mode to Enabled also works. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the attached project and run the scene. 2. Notice that the sprite's texture doesn't repeat, even though Default Texture Repeat is Enabled in the project settings. 3. Select the SubViewport and change Default Texture Repeat from Inherit to Enabled. 4. Run the scene again. The texture now repeats as expected. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [viewport-texture-repeat-inheritance-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32592406/viewport-texture-repeat-inheritance-mrp.zip)
